Primary_Symptoms: Neck stiffness and pain worsening with movement; Radiation to upper back; Suboccipital headache
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild shoulder aching; Reduced neck mobility; Muscle spasms in trapezius; Crepitus on neck rotation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard gardan tak hi hai ya haath me ja raha hai?; 2. Haath me sunn-pan ya kamzori hai?; 3. Computer/Mobile par lambe samay tak kaam karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD (if muscle spasm present); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs: max 7 days course. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer/GI bleed, kidney disease, severe heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma, and 3rd trimester pregnancy. Never combine two NSAIDs. Muscle relaxants Rx only (drowsiness caution, contraindicated in pregnancy/lactation)
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain proper ergonomic neck posture; Avoid prolonged forward head posture; Perform gentle neck isometric exercises once acute pain subsides; Use a thin firm cervical pillow; Avoid sudden neck twisting
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Cervical Spine (AP and Lateral views); MRI Cervical Spine (if neurological deficit present)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bowel/bladder control; Progressive weakness or loss of dexterity in hands; Unsteady gait/frequent falls; Sudden severe trauma

Common_Names_Hindi: Gardan se haath me dard; Cervical Radiculopathy
Primary_Symptoms: Sharp shooting electric-shock pain radiating from neck down the arm/forearm into fingers in a dermatomal pattern
Secondary_Symptoms: Numbness; Paresthesias (pins and needles); Weakness in specific arm/hand muscles; Reduced deep tendon reflexes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard gardan se chal kar haath ki ungliyo tak jata hai?; 2. Haath me suiya chubhna ya sunn-pan hai?; 3. Samaan pakadne me haath se chhoot-ta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Paracetamol
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Cervical collar short-term
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin are Rx only. Drowsiness, dizziness, and dependence caution; never stop abruptly. Oral NSAIDs caution in ulcers/renal disease. Doctor-administered cervical epidural steroid injections Rx only (limit injections, caution in diabetics)
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid heavy lifting and overhead activity; Use soft cervical collar for short periods during acute pain flares; Avoid traction or forceful neck manipulation; Sleep with proper neck support
Lab_Investigations: MRI Cervical Spine (Gold standard); Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive motor weakness in arm/hand (e.g., wrist drop, inability to grip); Sudden bowel or bladder dysfunction; Severe unremitting nocturnal pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Gardan me khichav; Postural Neck Pain
Primary_Symptoms: Aching stiffness and dull sore pain in back of neck and upper shoulders after prolonged desk/screen time
Secondary_Symptoms: Tension headaches; Upper back tightness; Muscle fatigue; Tenderness along trapezius
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Mobile/Laptop use karne ke baad gardan me dard badhta hai?; 2. Haath me koi sunn-pan ya dard to nahi jata?; 3. Aaram karne par teek hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Hot/Cold compress; Ergonomic adjustments
Precautions_Contraindications: Topical diclofenac gel and paracetamol are first-line OTC choices for mild pain. Stop and see a doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days. Avoid prolonged use of systemic NSAIDs without prescription
Home_Care_Advice: Take 5-minute movement breaks every 30 minutes of screen use; Elevate phone/screen to eye level; Perform hourly neck retractions (chin tucks) and shoulder rolls; Apply warm compresses for 15 minutes twice daily
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; No routine X-rays required unless red flags present
Emergency_Red_Flags: Fever with neck stiffness; Inability to touch chin to chest; Progressive arm weakness or numbness; Pain following high-velocity trauma

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe painful spasm of sternocleidomastoid muscle causing head to tilt to one side and rotate to opposite side
Secondary_Symptoms: Markedly restricted and painful neck rotation; Local tenderness; Muscle tightness; Mild headache
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Subah uthte hi achanak gardan ek taraf tedhi aur locked ho gayi hai?; 2. Gardan modne par severe painful spasm hota hai?; 3. Bukhar ya chot to nahi lagi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol + Thiocolchicoside OR Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Warm compresses; Soft cervical collar
Precautions_Contraindications: Muscle relaxants (Thiocolchicoside) are Rx only, max 5-7 days duration. Drowsiness and driving caution; STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING. Oral NSAIDs caution in peptic ulcer, renal disease, and asthma
Home_Care_Advice: Apply gentle moist heat compress to affected side for 15 minutes 3-4 times daily; Sleep on a supportive firm pillow; Avoid forced manual stretching or cracking of neck; Wear soft cervical collar temporarily for support
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; X-ray Cervical Spine (if history of trauma or persistent >1 week)
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with severe headache and neck stiffness (meningism); Dysphagia or difficulty breathing; History of neck trauma; Neurological deficits

Primary_Symptoms: Neck pain and stiffness developing within 24-48 hours after acceleration-deceleration injury (e.g., sudden motor vehicle impact)
Secondary_Symptoms: Headache (occipital); Decreased neck range of motion; Paresthesias in shoulders; Dizziness; Fatigue; Interscapular pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Gadi ke jhatke ya chot ke baad gardan me dard shuru hua hai?; 2. Haath me sunn-pan ya kamzori hai?; 3. Chakkar ya ulti aayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Soft cervical collar (short-term strictly <48h); Topical Diclofenac gel
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs max 5-7 days, take after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, renal failure, heart failure, and pregnancy. Stop and see doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days
Home_Care_Advice: Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for first 48 hours (15 mins 3 times daily); Maintain gentle gentle active movement as pain allows after 48h; Avoid prolonged rigid immobilization (delays recovery)
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Cervical Spine (rule out fracture/dislocation); MRI Cervical Spine (if severe pain, ligamentous injury suspected, or neurological signs)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of consciousness at time of injury; Progressive arm/leg weakness; Loss of bowel/bladder control; Severe vomiting or memory loss

Primary_Symptoms: Chronic lower back aching stiffness worsening after standing or prolonged bending; Local lumbar tenderness
Secondary_Symptoms: Morning back stiffness (<30 mins); Pain radiating to buttocks; Reduced spinal flexibility; Muscle fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ka dard kitne hafte se hai?; 2. Khade rehne ya jhukne par badhta hai?; 3. Pair me sunn-pan ya peshab ka control to nahi khoya?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Muscle relaxant (Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD if muscle spasm present); Core strengthening exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days), take after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, and pregnancy. Never combine two oral NSAIDs. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices
Home_Care_Advice: Red flags for back pain: loss of bladder/bowel control, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, trauma, unexplained weight loss, history of cancer. Maintain core muscle strengthening; Use lumbar support belt short-term during flares; Avoid lifting heavy loads with bent back
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Lumbar Spine (AP and Lateral views); MRI Lumbar Spine (if nerve compression or persistent pain >6 weeks)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Bladder or bowel incontinence/retention; Saddle anesthesia (numbness in groin/buttocks); Progressive foot drop or leg weakness; Fever with back pain; History of cancer with new back pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Kamar ka achanak khichav; Lumbar Sprain
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden sharp lower back pain immediately following heavy lifting, twisting, or sudden bending; Severe local muscle spasm
Secondary_Symptoms: Markedly restricted back movements; Difficulty standing straight; Antalgic tilt; Localized paraspinal tenderness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Wazan uthane ya achanak jhukne ke baad dard shuru hua?; 2. Kamar ki manspeshiya tight aur kadi lagti hain?; 3. Dard pair me niche to nahi ja raha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside OR Paracetamol + Chlorzoxazone
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Topical Diclofenac gel
Precautions_Contraindications: Muscle relaxants Rx only, max 5-7 days. Drowsiness and driving caution; Thiocolchicoside contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation. Oral NSAIDs short course after food, avoid in peptic ulcer/CKD
Home_Care_Advice: First 48h: ice wrapped in cloth for 15 mins 3-4 times daily; After 48h: warm compress; Rest on firm mattress in comfortable position with knees flexed; Early gentle walking as pain permits; Avoid heavy bending/lifting
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; X-ray Lumbar Spine only if severe trauma, red flags, or non-resolving after 2 weeks
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bladder/bowel control; Saddle numbness; Progressive leg weakness; High fever; Severe unremitting rest pain

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent or recurrent lower back pain lasting >12 weeks without a definitive structural/systemic cause identified
Secondary_Symptoms: General lumbar aching; Reduced functional capacity; Mild stiffness after inactivity; Associated anxiety or sleep disruption
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar dard 3 mahine se zyada se hai?; 2. Koi chot, bukhar ya pair me sunn-pan to nahi hai?; 3. Daily kaam-kaaj par kitna asar pad raha hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Naproxen (Short course during flares) + Exercise Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Duloxetine 30 mg OD (if chronic neuropathic/nociplastic pain under doctor); Core stability exercises; CBT
Precautions_Contraindications: Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC. Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days) after food; avoid continuous long-term daily NSAID use due to renal, gastric, and cardiovascular risks. PPI cover doctor-guided
Home_Care_Advice: Red flags: bladder/bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, fever, weight loss, cancer history. Stay active; avoid prolonged bed rest; Perform daily core strengthening and hamstring stretching exercises; Maintain healthy body weight
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Lumbar Spine; MRI Lumbar Spine (only to exclude specific spinal pathology if non-responsive); ESR/CRP
Emergency_Red_Flags: Bladder/bowel dysfunction; Saddle numbness; Unexplained weight loss; Progressive motor deficit in legs; Severe nocturnal pain

Primary_Symptoms: Sharp shooting back pain with nerve radiation into buttock, thigh, calf, or foot (Sciatica); Increased by coughing/sneezing
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Straight Leg Raise (SLR) test; Dermatomal paresthesias; Focal muscle weakness (e.g., extensor hallucis longus); Absent ankle jerk
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ka dard khansne ya chinkne par pair me niche jhatke se jata hai?; 2. Pair ya ungliyo me sunn-pan hai?; 3. Peshab karne me koi takleef hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Lumbo-sacral belt short-term
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin are Rx only, drowsiness/dependence caution; do not stop abruptly. Oral NSAIDs short course after food; contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure. Doctor-administered epidural steroid injection Rx only
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid forward bending, twisting, and lifting heavy weights; Maintain short periods of walking; Use firm mattress; Apply heat packs; Wear LS belt while walking short distances
Lab_Investigations: MRI Lumbar Spine (Gold standard for disc herniation and nerve root compression); X-ray Lumbar Spine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Cauda Equina Syndrome: sudden loss of bowel/bladder control, saddle numbness, bilateral severe leg weakness/foot drop (EMERGENCY SURGERY NEEDED)

Common_Names_Hindi: Sciatica; Pair me nass ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Burning, shooting, or electric-shock pain originating in lower back/buttock and traveling down back/side of leg to foot
Secondary_Symptoms: Leg numbness; Tingling sensation; Muscle weakness in foot/ankle; Pain exacerbated by sitting or coughing
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard kulhe (buttock) se hokar pair ke piche se aedi/ungliyo tak jata hai?; 2. Pair me sunn-pan ya chiintiya kat ti hain?; 3. Chhalne me pair kamzor lagta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Paracetamol
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Physiotherapy (nerve glides)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin and Gabapentin are Rx only; cause drowsiness, dizziness, and risk of dependence; never stop abruptly. NSAIDs short course after food. Oral steroids/epidural injections Rx only under specialist supervision
Home_Care_Advice: Red flags: bladder/bowel issues, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, trauma, weight loss, cancer history. Avoid prolonged sitting (>30 mins); Perform gentle neural mobilization/stretching exercises under guidance; Sleep with pillow between knees
Lab_Investigations: MRI Lumbosacral Spine; Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden bowel or bladder incontinence/retention; Saddle area numbness; Rapidly progressive leg weakness (e.g., foot drop); Severe unremitting rest pain

Primary_Symptoms: Lower back pain worsened by spinal extension (standing tall/bending backward) and relieved by sitting or forward flexion
Secondary_Symptoms: Hamstring tightness; Step-off palpation on lumbar spinous processes; Buttock aching; Neurogenic claudication if canal narrowed
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar piche jhukane ya lambe samay tak khade rehne par dard badhta hai?; 2. Baithne par aaram milta hai?; 3. X-ray me haddi khisaki hui batayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Core Rehabilitation
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Rigid Lumbo-sacral corset belt for activity; Physiotherapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, pregnancy. Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Avoid hyperextension exercises
Home_Care_Advice: Perform flexion-based core strengthening exercises (Williams flexion exercises); Avoid heavy weightlifting, backward bending, and high-impact jumping; Wear supportive LS belt during physical tasks
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Lumbar Spine (Flexion and Extension dynamic lateral views); MRI Lumbar Spine (assess spinal canal and neural foramina)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bowel/bladder control; Saddle numbness; Progressive neurological deficits in legs; Grade progression with severe unstable pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Kamar ki nali sikudna; Canal Stenosis
Primary_Symptoms: Neurogenic Claudication: bilateral leg pain, heaviness, numbness, or cramping appearing after walking a specific distance and RELIEVED BY SITTING/FORWARD BENDING
Secondary_Symptoms: Back pain; Relieved by leaning forward ('shopping cart sign'); Normal peripheral arterial pulses; Bilateral leg weakness on walking
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kuch door chalne par dono pairo me dard, sunn-pan, aur bhari-pan aata hai?; 2. Aage jhuk kar chalne ya baithne par 2 min me aaram milta hai?; 3. Pairo ki nasein (pulses) normal hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Pregabalin / Gabapentin + Physiotherapy / Epidural Steroid Injections / Surgical Decompression)
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Lumbar flexion physical therapy; Lumbar epidural steroid injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Pregabalin/Gabapentin Rx only; cause sedating effects. Differentiate neurogenic claudication (relieved by bending forward) from vascular claudication (relieved by standing still). Avoid spinal hyperextension
Home_Care_Advice: Walk with slight forward tilt or use a walking frame; Stationary cycling is well-tolerated; Avoid prolonged standing or walking upright; Maintain healthy weight
Lab_Investigations: MRI Lumbar Spine (Gold standard - cross-sectional canal area measurement); Plain Dynamic X-rays; Vascular Doppler (rule out PAD)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Cauda Equina Syndrome (bowel/bladder incontinence, saddle anesthesia); Progressive foot drop or leg weakness causing frequent falls

Primary_Symptoms: Inflammatory back pain in young adults (<45y): insidious onset, duration >3 months, MORNING STIFFNESS >30 MINS, IMPROVES WITH EXERCISE, WORSSENS WITH REST
Secondary_Symptoms: Alternating buttock pain; Enthesitis (Achilles tendon/plantar fascia pain); Uveitis (red painful eye); Reduced chest expansion; Bamboo spine
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Umar 45 se kam hai aur kamar me subah uthte hi 30 min se zyada aedan rehti hai?; 2. Kasrat karne par dard kam aur aaram karne par badhta hai?; 3. HLA-B27 test hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (First-line NSAIDs - Indomethacin / Etoricoxib; Biologics - TNF/IL-17 Inhibitors under Rheumatologist)
Supportive_Medicines: Sulfasalazine 500 mg BD (for peripheral joint involvement under rheumatologist); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Daily posture exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Long-term NSAIDs require strict monitoring for peptic ulcer, CKD, HTN, and cardiovascular events. Avoid prolonged spinal immobilization. Biologics require screening for latent TB and hepatitis B
Home_Care_Advice: Perform daily lifelong posture, spinal extension, and deep breathing exercises; Sleep flat on a firm mattress with a thin pillow; Complete smoking cessation (smoking accelerates spinal fusion)
Lab_Investigations: HLA-B27 gene test; MRI Sacroiliac Joints (detects early bone marrow edema/sacroiliitis); ESR and CRP (elevated); X-ray Pelvis with SI Joints
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe red painful eye with photophobia (Acute Anterior Uveitis - urgent eye referral); Spinal trauma with severe new neurological deficits (fracture of fused spine risk)

Primary_Symptoms: Unilateral or bilateral deep buttock pain originating from sacroiliac joint; Exacerbated by sitting, climbing stairs, or weight-bearing
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain radiating down posterior thigh (above knee); Local tenderness over SI joint sulcus; Positive Patrick/FABER test; Stiffness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kulhe (buttock) me andar tak tez dard hai?; 2. Ek pair par wazan daalne ya siidhiya chadne par badhta hai?; 3. Baithne par dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Naproxen
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Sacroiliac joint belt; Targeted SI joint steroid/local anesthetic injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. PPI cover doctor-guided. Steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid uneven weight-bearing, single-leg standing, and wide-stride lunges; Apply ice pack for 15 mins during acute pain; Wear SI supportive belt during standing/walking
Lab_Investigations: MRI Sacroiliac Joints (Gold standard); X-ray Pelvis with SI Joints; ESR/CRP; HLA-B27 testing
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with severe unilateral buttock pain (Septic Sacroiliitis suspicion); Neurological deficits in leg; Bowel/bladder dysfunction

Primary_Symptoms: Localized severe pain and tenderness at coccyx (tailbone); Exacerbated by prolonged sitting, sitting leaning back, or rising from a chair
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain on defecation or sexual intercourse; Local palpation tenderness over coccyx; Relieved by leaning forward while sitting
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ke sabse piche niche (tailbone) par baithne par tez dard hota hai?; 2. Kurse se uthte waqt ya piche tek lagane par badhta hai?; 3. Girne ya chot ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Etodolac / Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Cushion support (Coccyx wedge / Donut cushion); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Stool softeners (Syp Lactulose)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, renal disease, heart failure. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. Local corticosteroid/anesthetic injection Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Use a specialized donut-shaped or wedge-shaped coccyx cushion while sitting; Lean slightly forward while sitting to remove weight from tailbone; Apply ice packs for 15 mins 3 times daily; Use stool softeners to prevent straining during defecation
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Coccyx (Sitting and Standing dynamic views to check hypermobility/subluxation); MRI Coccyx (if persistent non-responsive pain)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Fever with local redness/swelling/pus discharge (Pilonidal abscess or bone infection); Rectal bleeding; Unexplained weight loss

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden involuntary, painful contraction and tightness of lumbar paraspinal muscles; Locked or rigid low back posture
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe local tenderness; Inability to bend or straighten back comfortably; Dull aching residual pain after acute spasm subsides
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ki manspeshi achanak kadi aur tez dard waali ho gayi hai?; 2. Jhukne ya hilne me takleef hai?; 3. Pain pair me to nahi ja raha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol + Thiocolchicoside OR Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Warm compresses; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: Muscle relaxants (Thiocolchicoside) Rx only, max 5-7 days. Drowsiness and driving caution; STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING. NSAIDs short course after food
Home_Care_Advice: Apply cold pack for first 24 hours, followed by warm compresses for 15 minutes 3-4 times daily; Gentle active walking as tolerated; Avoid absolute bed rest beyond 1 day; Avoid heavy lifting
Lab_Investigations: Red flags for back pain: loss of bladder/bowel control, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, trauma, weight loss, cancer history. Clinical evaluation; Imaging usually not required for simple uncomplicated spasm
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bowel or bladder control; Saddle numbness; Severe shooting leg pain with numbness; High fever

Primary_Symptoms: Mid-back aching pain and muscle tightness between shoulder blades; Worsened by prolonged slouched sitting or desk work
Secondary_Symptoms: Tenderness along rhomboid and thoracic erector spinae muscles; Restrictive chest tightness feeling; Postural fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pith (dono kulho/shoulders ke beech) me dard rehta hai?; 2. Computer par kaam karte hue ya jhukne par badhta hai?; 3. Saans lene me chhati me dard to nahi hota?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Postural correction brace (short-term); Scapular retraction exercises; Warm compresses
Precautions_Contraindications: Topical diclofenac gel and paracetamol are first-line OTC choices for mild pain. Stop and see a doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days. Avoid prolonged use of systemic NSAIDs without prescription
Home_Care_Advice: Take regular movement breaks during desk work; Perform scapular squeezes and thoracic extension stretches; Optimize workstation ergonomics; Avoid slouching
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Thoracic Spine (AP and Lateral views - rule out compression fracture or Scheuermann's disease if persistent)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Pain radiating around chest wall triggered by exertion (rule out cardiac origin); Progressive lower limb numbness/weakness; Fever with thoracic pain; History of major trauma or cancer

Common_Names_Hindi: Jhuki hui pith ka dard; Kyphosis
Primary_Symptoms: Aching discomfort and muscular fatigue in upper mid-back due to exaggerated forward rounding (hump) of thoracic spine
Secondary_Symptoms: Postural muscle strain; Decreased spinal mobility; Suboccipital tension headaches; Prominent vertebral spinous processes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pith piche se gol/jhuki hui (hump) lagti hai?; 2. Lambe samay tak baithne par pith me thakan aur dard hota hai?; 3. Umar kitni hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Ibuprofen (Short course for flares)
Supportive_Medicines: Postural strengthening exercises; Thoracic extension bracing (in adolescents with Scheuermann's disease under specialist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-5 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma, and 3rd trimester pregnancy. Never combine two NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Perform thoracic extension and core strengthening exercises daily; Avoid slouching; Use ergonomic lumbar/thoracic supportive chairs; Maintain adequate Calcium and Vitamin D levels
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Thoracic Spine (Lateral view - Cobb angle measurement); Bone Mineral Density DEXA scan (in elderly to rule out osteoporotic fracture)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly worsening spinal deformity; New onset leg weakness or numbness; Difficulty breathing due to severe thoracic restriction; Unexplained weight loss

Primary_Symptoms: Aching back pain and muscular asymmetry due to abnormal lateral (side-to-side) curvature of spine
Secondary_Symptoms: Uneven shoulder heights; Prominent rib hump on forward bending (Adams forward bend test); Asymmetric waistline; Fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Reeth ki haddi ek taraf tedhi (S-shape/C-shape) lagti hai?; 2. Ek taraf ka shoulder ya kulha upar-niche hai?; 3. Peeth me ek taraf ki manspeshiyo me khichav hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac (Short course for flares) + Exercise Rehabilitation
Supportive_Medicines: Specialized Scoliosis Physiotherapy (Schroth method); Custom spinal bracing (in growing adolescents under specialist); Core strengthening
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Avoid prolonged unmonitored NSAID use. Severe progressive curves require specialist spine surgery consultation
Home_Care_Advice: Perform asymmetrical core and back strengthening exercises under physical therapist guidance; Maintain active lifestyle and swimming; Avoid high-impact asymmetrical axial loading
Lab_Investigations: Full-spine standing X-rays (AP and Lateral views - Cobb angle measurement); MRI Spine (if atypical curve, rapid progression, or neurological signs)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive shortness of breath or chest restriction; Rapid progression of spinal curve; New onset leg weakness, numbness, or loss of bowel/bladder control

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden loss of bowel or bladder control (urinary retention/overflow incontinence, fecal incontinence); Saddle anesthesia (numbness in groin/perineum/buttocks)
Secondary_Symptoms: Progressive bilateral leg weakness/numbness; Severe lower back and bilateral sciatica pain; Sexual dysfunction; Foot drop
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peshab ya latrine ka control bilkul khoy gaya hai ya peshab ruka hai?; 2. Guptang aur hips ke paas sunn-pan (saddle numbness) hai?; 3. Dono pairo me kamzori hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Methylprednisolone / IV Analgesics in ER
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate emergency Transfer to Tertiary Spine Surgery Center; Emergency MRI Spine; Surgical Lumbar Decompression / Discectomy within 24-48 hours to prevent permanent paralysis
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening surgical emergency. Do NOT attempt home care, massage, or spinal manipulation. Immediate emergency surgical evaluation required
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital referral to a spine surgery center; Keep patient flat on stretcher; Do NOT give anything by mouth (NPO) as emergency surgery is likely
Lab_Investigations: Urgent Emergency MRI Lumbar Spine (Gold standard); Post-void residual bladder scan; Neurological examination
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Sudden loss of bladder or bowel control; Saddle anesthesia (numbness in groin/buttocks); Progressive bilateral leg weakness/paralysis

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset severe localized mid-to-lower back pain following minor trauma, fall, or spontaneously in severe osteoporosis
Secondary_Symptoms: Point tenderness over spinous process; Markedly restricted mobility; Pain worsening with any movement or coughing; Height loss; Kyphosis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Achanak girne, jhatke, ya severe osteoporosis ke baad tez kamar/pith me dard hua?; 2. Haddi ke upar dabane par severe dard hota hai?; 3. Khade hone me takleef hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral (Paracetamol / Calcitonin / Brace / Kyphoplasty evaluation)
Supportive_Medicines: Rigid Spinal Orthosis (TLSO brace); Anti-osteoporotic therapy (Teriparatide / Bisphosphonates); Kyphoplasty/Vertebroplasty evaluation
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Emergency hospital referral needed to rule out spinal cord/nerve compression. Do NOT force movement or stretch the back. Avoid NSAIDs if kidney failure or advanced age
Home_Care_Advice: Immobilize patient on a firm flat surface; Avoid twisting, bending, or sitting upright until evaluated; Apply cold compresses wrapped in cloth; Transfer to hospital for X-ray/MRI
Lab_Investigations: Emergency X-ray Thoracolumbar Spine; MRI Spine (differentiates acute vs old fracture, checks nerve compression); DEXA Scan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: New onset leg weakness or numbness; Loss of bowel or bladder control; Inability to void urine; Severe unremitting trauma pain

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent localized back pain with evening rise of fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, and anorexia; Localized gibbus deformity
Secondary_Symptoms: Local spinous tenderness; Cold abscess in groin/flank; Neurological deficits (paraplegia/paraparesis); Spinal stiffness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar me purana dard hai aur shaam ko bukhar, raat ko pasiina, ya weight kam ho raha hai?; 2. Pith par koi ubhaar (gibbus/hump) bana hai?; 3. Pair me kamzori hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (National Anti-Tubercular Therapy - Rifampicin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol)
Adult_Strength_Mg: Per body weight (Rifampicin 450-600 mg, Isoniazid 300 mg)
Meal_Timing: Empty Stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after food)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (9 to 12 months)
Supportive_Medicines: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) 10-20 mg OD; Spinal bracing (TLSO / LS belt); Liver function monitoring
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Anti-tubercular drugs are Rx only. Rifampicin causes orange-red discoloration of urine/tears. Isoniazid requires Pyridoxine co-prescription to prevent peripheral neuropathy. Monitor LFTs monthly
Home_Care_Advice: Take ATT strictly on empty stomach every morning without missing doses; Wear spinal brace while sitting/standing; Eat high-protein nutritious diet; Regular follow-up with spine specialist
Lab_Investigations: MRI Spine with Contrast (Gold standard); CT-guided Biopsy / GeneXpert (CBNAAT) for Mycobacterium tuberculosis; ESR and CRP (markedly elevated); Chest X-ray
Emergency_Red_Flags: Onset of leg weakness, numbness, or inability to walk (Pott's paraplegia); Sudden loss of bowel or bladder control; Kyphotic angle breakdown

Primary_Symptoms: Progressive global restriction of both ACTIVE and PASSIVE shoulder movements (especially external rotation); Severe nocturnal shoulder pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain sleeping on affected side; Pain stages: Freezing (painful), Frozen (stiff), Thawing (recovery); Deltoid muscle atrophy
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kandha bilkul jam ho gaya hai aur doosre haath se bhi nahi ghoomta?; 2. Raat ko kandhe ke bhal sote samay severe dard hota hai?; 3. Diabetes ya thyroid hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Naproxen
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Intra-articular corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered); Hydrodilatation
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, 3rd trimester pregnancy. Intra-articular steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered only (caution in diabetics as it spikes blood sugar)
Home_Care_Advice: Perform gentle pendulum exercises and wall-climbing finger stretches 3 times daily within pain-free range; Apply warm compresses before stretching; Avoid forced aggressive sudden pulls
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Shoulder (AP and Axillary views - rule out glenohumeral arthritis/calcification); MRI Shoulder / Ultrasound (exclude rotator cuff tear); HbA1c & TSH
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe swelling, redness, and high fever in shoulder joint (Septic Arthritis suspicion); Complete loss of sensation in arm

Common_Names_Hindi: Kandhe ki nass me sujan; Rotator Cuff
Primary_Symptoms: Anterolateral shoulder pain exacerbated by overhead activities (reaching, lifting, combing hair); Painful arc between 60°-120° abduction
Secondary_Symptoms: Night pain when lying on affected arm; Local tenderness over greater tuberosity; Muscle weakness on resisted elevation; Preserved passive ROM
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath ko upar uthane ya piche le jane par kandhe me dard hota hai?; 2. Raat ko kandhe ke bhal sone par dard badhta hai?; 3. Overhead kaam karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Naproxen / Ibuprofen
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Subacromial steroid injection (specialist-administered); Rotator cuff physical therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (5-7 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. Subacromial steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid overhead lifting, reaching behind back, and sleeping directly on affected shoulder; Apply ice pack for 15 mins 3 times daily during acute phase; Perform rotator cuff isometric strengthening once acute pain subsides
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Shoulder; MRI Shoulder (evaluates tendon tears/tendinopathy); X-ray Shoulder (AP and Supraspinatus outlet views)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden inability to raise arm (acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear); Severe swelling, redness, and high fever in shoulder

Primary_Symptoms: Painful arc of shoulder motion (pain between 60°-120° abduction) caused by subacromial bursal/tendon compression under acromion
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Neer's and Hawkins-Kennedy tests; Anterolateral shoulder pain; Night pain; Grinding sensation on overhead movement
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath 60 se 120 degree ke beech uthane par kandhe me tez dard hota hai?; 2. Haath niche ya poora upar karne par dard kam hota hai?; 3. Overhead kaam karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Subacromial Decompression Rehab
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Subacromial corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered); Scapular stabilization therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. Subacromial steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered (limit total injections to prevent tendon weakening)
Home_Care_Advice: Modify activities to avoid repeated overhead arm positions; Apply ice packs for 15 mins after activity; Perform scapular retractor strengthening and posterior capsule stretching exercises
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Shoulder (AP, Axillary, and Outlet views - checks acromial morphology/spurs); Ultrasound Shoulder; MRI Shoulder
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden arm drop or inability to abduct arm actively; Severe joint swelling with high fever and chills

Common_Names_Hindi: Kandhe ki thaili me sujan; Bursitis
Primary_Symptoms: Acute severe anterolateral shoulder pain with localized swelling and severe tenderness over subacromial space; Pain with all movements
Secondary_Symptoms: Marked restriction of overhead movements; Severe nocturnal pain preventing sleep on affected side; Warmth over subacromial area
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kandhe ke bahar/upar ki taraf severe dard aur choone par sujan hai?; 2. Haath hilane par aur raat ko sote me dard badhta hai?; 3. Achanak shuru hua?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Naproxen / Etoricoxib
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Subacromial bursa corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered); Ice therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs max 5-7 days after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma, 3rd trimester pregnancy. Never combine two NSAIDs. Subacromial steroid injection Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Rest affected arm; Apply ice pack wrapped in towel for 15-20 minutes 3-4 times daily; Avoid overhead activities and lifting; Use an arm sling short-term (1-2 days) for acute pain relief
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Shoulder (Gold standard for subacromial bursal fluid accumulation); X-ray Shoulder; MRI Shoulder
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly spreading erythema, severe warmth, high fever, and systemic chills (Septic Bursitis - urgent drainage/antibiotics needed)

Primary_Symptoms: Anterior shoulder pain localized strictly over bicipital groove; Pain worsened by flexion of elbow/shoulder against resistance
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Speed's and Yergason's tests; Local tenderness over anterior shoulder; Pain during pulling or lifting objects
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kandhe ke aage ki taraf (biceps muscle ke upar) dard hai?; 2. Haath ko modne ya wazan uthane par dard badhta hai?; 3. Aage choone par dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Ibuprofen
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Biceps tendon sheath steroid injection (specialist-administered); Physiotherapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, asthma, pregnancy. Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Steroid injections directly into long head of biceps tendon should be done cautiously by specialists due to rupture risk
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid repetitive arm curling, pulling, and overhead weightlifting; Apply ice packs for 15 mins 3 times daily; Perform gentle bicipital stretching once acute pain subsides
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Shoulder (visualizes long head of biceps tendon and fluid in sheath); MRI Shoulder; X-ray Shoulder
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden 'pop' sensation in anterior arm with bulging biceps muscle belly ('Popeye muscle' deformity - distal/proximal biceps tendon rupture)

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe shoulder pain and complete inability to move joint following trauma; 'Squared-off' shoulder appearance with empty glenoid
Secondary_Symptoms: Prominent acromion process; Patient holds injured arm in slight abduction and external rotation; Axillary nerve numbness over deltoid badge area
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chot ya girne ke baad kandha achanak apni jagah se nikal gaya hai?; 2. Kandha bilkul hil nahi raha aur aakar badal gaya hai?; 3. Haath me sunn-pan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Tramadol / Injection Midazolam + Fentanyl (for procedural sedation during reduction in ER)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate closed reduction under procedural sedation in ER by Orthopedic Surgeon
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER Transfer; X-ray confirmation; Closed Reduction; Shoulder immobilizer sling for 2-3 weeks post-reduction; Rehabilitation
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening joint emergency. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO FORCEFULLY PULL OR REDUCE THE DISLOCATED SHOULDER AT HOME (risk of fracture, nerve damage, or vascular tear)
Home_Care_Advice: Immobilize injured arm against chest using a sling or folded cloth; Apply ice pack wrapped in towel; Do NOT give anything by mouth (NPO) as sedation/anesthesia is needed for reduction
Lab_Investigations: Emergency X-ray Shoulder (AP and Scapular-Y views - mandatory before and after reduction); CT Shoulder (if complex fracture-dislocation)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Complete loss of sensation over deltoid badge area (axillary nerve injury); Cold, pale hand with absent radial pulse (subclavian/axillary artery compromise)

Common_Names_Hindi: AC Joint Pain; AC Joint arthritis
Primary_Symptoms: Localized pain at top of shoulder over acromioclavicular (AC) joint; Exacerbated by cross-body arm adduction (reaching across chest)
Secondary_Symptoms: Local tenderness over AC joint; Positive cross-arm adduction test; Prominence of distal clavicle (if post-traumatic step-off); Pain sleeping on side
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kandhe ke sabse upar patti/haddi par dard hai?; 2. Haath ko doosre kandhe ki taraf samne se le jane par dard badhta hai?; 3. Wazan uthane par dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Local Care
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; AC joint corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered); Shoulder strap support
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Intra-articular AC joint steroid injection Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid cross-body arm reaching, bench press, and heavy overhead lifting; Apply ice pack for 15 mins twice daily; Wear supportive shoulder sling short-term during acute flares
Lab_Investigations: X-ray AC Joint (Zanca view - checks joint space narrowing, osteophytes, or distal clavicle osteolysis); Ultrasound AC Joint
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe step-off deformity at top of shoulder following trauma (Grade III-VI AC joint separation); High fever with localized joint redness

Common_Names_Hindi: Tennis Elbow; Koni ke bahar ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Burning pain and tenderness over lateral epicondyle of elbow; Exacerbated by resisted wrist extension, gripping, or wringing clothes
Secondary_Symptoms: Weakness in grip strength; Localized point tenderness 1 cm distal to lateral epicondyle; Positive Cozen's and Mill's tests; Morning stiffness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koni ke bahar ki taraf choone par tez dard hota hai?; 2. Kapaad nichodne, taala kholne, ya wazan uthane par dard badhta hai?; 3. Computer mouse/repetitive work karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Naproxen + Tennis Elbow Strap
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Counterforce Tennis Elbow brace/strap; Corticosteroid / PRP injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (5-7 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. Paracetamol and topical diclofenac gel first-line OTC choices. Steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered (use sparingly as repeated injections weaken tendon)
Home_Care_Advice: Wear a counterforce Tennis Elbow strap placed 2 inches below elbow joint during manual tasks; Avoid repetitive wrist extension and heavy gripping; Apply ice pack for 15 mins 3 times daily; Perform eccentric wrist extensor strengthening exercises
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Elbow (visualizes extensor carpi radialis brevis tendinopathy); X-ray Elbow (AP and Lateral views - rules out radiocapitellar arthritis or calcification)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden inability to extend fingers or wrist (radial nerve compromise); Severe elbow joint swelling with high fever

Common_Names_Hindi: Golfer's Elbow; Koni ke andar ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Pain and tenderness localized over medial epicondyle of elbow; Exacerbated by resisted wrist flexion and forearm pronation
Secondary_Symptoms: Reduced grip strength; Stiffness in elbow; Paresthesias in 4th and 5th fingers if ulnar nerve irritated; Pain on lifting objects palm-up
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koni ke andar ki taraf (body ki side) choone par dard hai?; 2. Haath ki hatheli ko andar modne ya wazan pakadne par dard badhta hai?; 3. Repetitive arm tasks karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Ibuprofen
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Medial counterforce brace; Corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, 3rd trimester pregnancy. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. Local steroid injection Rx and doctor-administered (caution near ulnar nerve)
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid repetitive wrist flexing, forceful palm-up lifting, and wringing actions; Wear counterforce strap below elbow; Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 mins 3 times daily; Perform wrist flexor stretching
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Elbow (evaluates flexor pronator tendon origin); X-ray Elbow; Nerve Conduction Velocity (if ulnar neuropathy symptoms present)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive numbness or weakness in ring and little fingers; Severe swelling with high fever and joint redness

Common_Names_Hindi: Koni par paani ki thaili; Bursitis
Primary_Symptoms: Focal swelling ('goose egg') over posterior tip of elbow (olecranon); Fluctuant, soft, fluid-filled sac; Mild or no pain if non-septic
Secondary_Symptoms: Erythema; Warmth and severe tenderness (if septic); Restricted extreme elbow flexion due to tightness; Local pressure discomfort
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koni ke piche achanak gol, paani bhari soojan (egg-like) ban gayi hai?; 2. Soojan lal, garam, aur severe dard waali hai?; 3. Koni par chot lagi thi ya atek kar baithte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol (if aseptic) OR Antibiotics + Aspiration (if Septic Bursitis under Doctor)
Dosage_Frequency: BD (Aceclofenac) / TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / TDS (Augmentin if septic)
Duration_Days: 5 to 7 days (NSAIDs) / 7 to 10 days (Antibiotics if septic)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Elbow compression bandage; Needle aspiration and fluid analysis (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course for aseptic bursitis. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, pregnancy. SEPTIC BURSITIS REQUIRES URGENT DOCTOR EVALUATION AND PRESCRIPTION ANTIBIOTICS. Do NOT perform home needle aspiration
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid resting elbows on hard surfaces; Wear protective elbow elbow pad or cushion; Apply ice pack wrapped in towel for 15 mins 3 times daily; Apply light compression wrap
Lab_Investigations: Bursal Fluid Aspiration (Gram stain, cell count, crystal analysis, and culture); X-ray Elbow (rule out olecranon spur or fracture)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Rapidly spreading redness, extreme warmth, severe pain, purulent discharge, and high fever with chills (Septic Bursitis requiring emergency surgical drainage)

Common_Names_Hindi: Koni me nass dabna; Cubital Tunnel
Primary_Symptoms: Paresthesias (numbness, tingling) and pain in ring and little fingers (4th and 5th digits) and ulnar border of hand
Secondary_Symptoms: Weakness of hand grip and pinch strength; Clawing of 4th and 5th digits (ulnar claw hand); Positive Tinel's sign at cubital tunnel; Worsened by prolonged elbow flexion
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath ki aakhri do ungliyo (ring aur little finger) me sunn-pan aur chiintiya kat ti hain?; 2. Koni mod kar rakhne par (phone par baat karte hue) badhta hai?; 3. Haath se samaan chhoot-ta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Night Elbow Splint
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Nighttime elbow extension splint; Physical therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin and Gabapentin are Rx only; drowsiness, dizziness, and dependence caution; never stop abruptly. Avoid forced elbow flexion. Surgical ulnar nerve transposition Rx under specialist if conservative therapy fails
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid keeping elbow bent at acute angles (>90°) for prolonged periods (e.g., sleeping with bent arms, holding phone); Wear a soft night extension splint keeping elbow straight; Use hands-free phone speaker
Lab_Investigations: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS) and Electromyography (EMG - confirms ulnar nerve compression at elbow); Ultrasound Ulnar Nerve
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive wasting (atrophy) of intrinsic hand muscles (first dorsal interosseous); Loss of hand dexterity; Severe unremitting numbness

Common_Names_Hindi: Kalai me nass dabna; Carpal Tunnel
Primary_Symptoms: Numbness, tingling, and burning pain in thumb, index, middle, and radial half of ring finger, WORST AT NIGHT (awakens patient from sleep)
Secondary_Symptoms: Paresthesias relieved by 'shaking' hands; Positive Phalen's and Tinel's tests; Weakness of thumb abduction; Thenar muscle atrophy (late stage)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Raat ko sote me haath ki shuruaati 3-4 ungliyo me sunn-pan aur dard se neend khulti hai?; 2. Haath jhatakne (shaking) par aaram milta hai?; 3. Computer typing ya repetitive work karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Volar Wrist Splint
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Volar wrist cock-up splint (worn at night); Carpal tunnel local corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin Rx only, drowsiness and dependence caution; do not stop abruptly. Local carpal tunnel steroid injection Rx and doctor-administered only (caution in diabetics). Surgical carpal tunnel release Rx for refractory cases
Home_Care_Advice: Wear a neutral volar wrist cock-up splint continuously at night; Take regular wrist breaks during repetitive typing/mouse use; Avoid repetitive wrist flexion and heavy vibration tools; Perform median nerve gliding exercises
Lab_Investigations: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS) and Electromyography (EMG - Gold standard); Ultrasound Median Nerve; HbA1c and TSH (screen for co-existing diabetes/hypothyroidism)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Visible flattening/wasting (atrophy) of thenar muscle base of thumb; Loss of thumb opposition strength; Permanent sensory loss

Primary_Symptoms: Severe pain and swelling over radial styloid process at base of thumb; Worsened by thumb movement and wrist ulnar deviation
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Finkelstein's test (sharp pain when making a fist over tucked thumb and bending wrist toward little finger); Local tenderness; Crepitus
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Angoothe ke niche kalai par choone par tez dard hota hai?; 2. Angoothe ko andar dabakar kalai modne par severe pain hota hai?; 3. Bachhe ko uthane ya wazan pakadne par badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Thumb Spica Splint
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Rigid Thumb Spica splint; First extensor compartment corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. Local corticosteroid injection Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Wear a rigid Thumb Spica immobilizing splint during daily activities and sleep; Avoid repetitive thumb pinching, wringing, and lifting heavy objects with outstretched thumbs; Apply ice pack for 15 mins 3 times daily
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Wrist (evaluates APL and EPB tendons and sheath thickening); X-ray Wrist (AP and Lateral - rules out scaphoid/trapezium pathology)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe unremitting pain preventing all hand function; Local skin erythema, pus, and fever

Primary_Symptoms: Painful clicking, catching, or locking of a finger/thumb in flexion during movement; Finger must be manually straightened with a 'pop'
Secondary_Symptoms: Painful nodule felt over A1 pulley at palmar crease base of affected finger; Morning stiffness in fingers; Restricted digit extension
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ungli modne ke baad seedhi karne par aatankti (lock hoti) hai?; 2. Ungli seedhi karne par 'pop' ya jhatka lagta hai?; 3. Hatheli ke paas gummda choone par dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Finger Splint
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Night finger extension splint; A1 pulley corticosteroid injection (specialist-administered); A1 pulley release surgery
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. Local A1 pulley steroid injection Rx and doctor-administered (caution in diabetics)
Home_Care_Advice: Wear a finger extension splint at night to keep digit straight; Perform gentle passive finger stretching in warm water in the morning; Avoid repetitive tight hand gripping and squeezing tools
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Finger (evaluates A1 pulley thickening and flexor tendon nodule); Plain X-ray Hand (rule out joint pathology)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Finger permanently locked in flexed position that cannot be straightened passively; High fever with palmar flexor sheath redness and purulent swelling

Primary_Symptoms: Soft, smooth, transilluminable, non-tender or mildly aching fluid-filled subcutaneous lump on dorsal or volar wrist / base of finger
Secondary_Symptoms: Fluctuant mass attached to underlying joint capsule/tendon sheath; Size changes with activity; Occasional local nerve pressure pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kalai par soft, gol, paani waala gummda (lump) bana hai?; 2. Light jalane par roshni aar-paar hoti hai (transillumination)?; 3. Vard badhta hai kaam karne par?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Reassurance (No Drug Required) OR Aceclofenac (if symptomatic pain)
Supportive_Medicines: Wrist supportive splint; Needle aspiration and steroid instillation (specialist-administered); Surgical excision
Precautions_Contraindications: Reassurance is primary management as ganglion cysts are completely benign. DO NOT HIT THE CYST WITH A HEAVY BOOK (historic 'Bible therapy' causes severe tissue injury and bone fracture). Aspiration/Surgery Rx under specialist
Home_Care_Advice: Reassure patient regarding benign nature; Avoid repetitive strenuous wrist loading if painful; Wear a supportive wrist brace during heavy manual work
Lab_Investigations: Transillumination test (positive); Ultrasound Wrist (confirms cystic nature); MRI Wrist (if occult or diagnostic doubt)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden rapid increase in size with severe joint pain; Compression of median or ulnar nerve causing progressive sensory/motor deficit

Primary_Symptoms: Painless nodular thickening and cord formation of palmar fascia leading to progressive flexor contracture of fingers (4th and 5th digits)
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to place hand flat on a table ('table-top test' positive); Skin puckering on palm; Fixed flexed posture of MP and PIP joints
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Hatheli par kadi patti/ganth bani hai jo ungliyo ko andar mod rahi hai?; 2. Hatheli ko meez par flat rakhne par nahi tikti?; 3. Dard nahi hota par ungli seedhi nahi hoti?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: No Primary Oral Drug Effective (Surgical / Enzymatic intervention under Specialist)
Supportive_Medicines: Collagenase clostridium histolyticum injection (specialist-administered); Fasciectomy / Needle aponeurotomy (Hand Surgeon)
Precautions_Contraindications: No oral medications cure or reverse Dupuytren's contracture. DO NOT FORCEFULLY STRETCH OR PULL FLEXED FINGERS (causes tendon/nerve injury). Specialist hand surgery evaluation recommended when hand cannot lay flat
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain hand hygiene in deep flexed palmar creases; Avoid aggressive manual stretching; Consult hand surgeon if contracture interferes with daily activities (washing face, wearing gloves)
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation ('Table-top test'); Hand X-ray (rule out joint bony pathology)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapid progression of contracture preventing basic hygiene; Neurovascular impairment in fingers

Primary_Symptoms: Acute wrist pain, localized swelling, bruising, and tenderness following a fall on an outstretched hand (FOOSH) or sudden twisting
Secondary_Symptoms: Decreased wrist ROM; Localized ecchymosis; Pain worsened by wrist flexion/extension; Absence of bony deformity
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath ke bhal girne ke baad kalai me dard aur soojan aayi hai?; 2. Kalai me koi tedha-pan ya bhayankar dard to nahi hai?; 3. Choone par haddi par tez dard hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Ibuprofen + RICE Protocol
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Wrist immobilizer brace; Elastic crepe bandage
Precautions_Contraindications: First-line for mild/moderate sprain: RICE protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) and early gentle movement as pain allows. Avoid heat and massage in first 48h. Oral NSAIDs short course after food. X-ray mandatory if unable to bear weight or tenderness over scaphoid anatomical snuffbox
Home_Care_Advice: Follow RICE protocol: Rest wrist in brace, apply Ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 mins 3-4 times daily, apply light Compression crepe bandage, Elevate wrist above heart level; Avoid heat/massage for 48 hours
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Wrist (AP, Lateral, and Scaphoid views - MUST RULE OUT SCAPHOID FRACTURE); Ultrasound / MRI Wrist (if chronic instability or ligament tear suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe point tenderness in anatomical snuffbox (Scaphoid fracture risk); Visible wrist deformity; Cold, pale hand or thumb numbness

Primary_Symptoms: Pain, swelling, erythema, and tenderness along the course of a tendon sheath; Pain exacerbated by active contraction or passive stretch
Secondary_Symptoms: Crepitus on tendon movement; Localized warmth; Restricted joint ROM; Palpable fluid accumulation along tendon
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Nass ki patti ke sath soojan, lalapan, aur chalane par dard hota hai?; 2. Nass ko hilane par 'charcharahat' (crepitus) mehsoos hoti hai?; 3. Repetitive kaam ya infection ke baad hua?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Immobilization
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Supportive splinting; Local corticosteroid injection (if non-infectious, under specialist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. INFECTIOUS TENOSYNOVITIS (Kanavel's cardinal signs) IS A SURGICAL EMERGENCY REQUIRING URGENT HOSPITAL ADMISSION AND IV ANTIBIOTICS
Home_Care_Advice: Rest affected tendon using a supportive splint; Apply ice pack for 15 mins 3 times daily during non-infectious flares; Avoid repetitive straining activities
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Tendon (evaluates sheath fluid and synovial thickening); X-ray; Inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP); Wound/fluid culture if infectious
Emergency_Red_Flags: Kanavel's 4 signs of Infectious Flexor Tenosynovitis: digit fixed in flexion, symmetric sausage-like finger swelling, tenderness along entire tendon sheath, severe pain on passive extension (URGENT SURGERY NEEDED)

Primary_Symptoms: Compression of neurovascular bundle (brachial plexus / subclavian vessels) at thoracic outlet; Arm paresthesias, pain, and weakness
Secondary_Symptoms: Vascular TOS: pale/cyanotic hand, cold extremity, absent radial pulse on arm elevation (Adson's test); Neurogenic TOS: paresthesias in C8-T1 distribution
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath upar uthane par poore haath me sunn-pan, dard ya haath ka neela/thanda padna hota hai?; 2. Garadan aur shoulder ke paas khichav hai?; 3. Extra collar bone (cervical rib) hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Physical Therapy (Neurogenic TOS)
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Postural physical therapy; Surgical cervical rib excision / scalenectomy (specialist referral)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin Rx only; drowsiness caution. Vascular TOS (subclavian vein thrombosis / subclavian artery aneurysm) requires urgent vascular surgery evaluation and anticoagulation/surgery. Avoid heavy shoulder bags
Home_Care_Advice: Perform shoulder girdle elevation and posture correction exercises; Avoid carrying heavy shoulder bags or backpacks; Avoid prolonged overhead positioning of arms
Lab_Investigations: Cervical Spine and Chest X-rays (rule out Cervical Rib); MRI / CT Angiography Head & Neck; Electromyography (EMG) and NCS; Arterial/Venous Doppler Ultrasound
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden cold, pale, painful, pulseless arm (acute arterial occlusion); Sudden blue swollen painful arm (Paget-Schroetter syndrome - subclavian vein thrombosis); Rapid muscle wasting

Primary_Symptoms: Diffuse aching pain, stiffness, muscle fatigue, and mild tingling in forearm, wrist, neck, or shoulder from repetitive computer work
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild swelling; Loss of grip endurance; Tenderness along forearm flexor/extensor muscle bellies; Worsened toward end of workday
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Computer mouse/typing karne ke baad forearm, kalai ya gardan me dard badhta hai?; 2. Haath me thakan aur kamzori mehsoos hoti hai?; 3. Ergonomic setup kaisa hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel + Ergonomic Redesign
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Topical NSAID gel; Ergonomic mouse/keyboard; Forearm stretching exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Topical diclofenac gel and paracetamol are first-line OTC choices. Stop and see doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days. Avoid prolonged systemic NSAID use. Modify workplace ergonomics as definitive cure
Home_Care_Advice: Follow 20-20-20 rule (every 20 mins look 20 feet away for 20 secs); Use vertical ergonomic mouse and padded wrist rests; Keep elbows at 90° and wrists neutral while typing; Perform regular forearm stretches
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; NCS/EMG (rule out Carpal/Cubital Tunnel Syndrome if focal numbness persists)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive motor weakness in hand; Persistent midnight awakening pain; Severe joint redness or swelling

Primary_Symptoms: Localized muscle pain, stiffness, and tenderness in upper limb (biceps, triceps, forearm) following sudden overload or overstretching
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain worsened by active muscle contraction or passive stretch; Mild localized swelling; Muscle weakness; Ecchymosis (bruising)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heavy lifting ya exercise ke baad baju ki manspeshi me jhatka/dard hua hai?; 2. Baju modne ya sidhi karne par dard badhta hai?; 3. Soojan ya neela-pan aaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + RICE Protocol
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Elastic compression bandage; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: First-line for muscle strains: RICE protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) and early gentle movement as pain allows; avoid heat and massage in first 48 hours. Oral NSAIDs short course after food
Home_Care_Advice: Follow RICE protocol: Rest arm, apply Ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 mins 3-4 times daily for first 48h, light Compression wrap, Elevate limb; Avoid direct heat/deep massage for 48 hours
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; Ultrasound Muscle (if large hematoma or complete muscle tear suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Visible muscle belly gap or 'pop' sensation (complete muscle tendon rupture); Rapidly expanding tense painful swelling (Compartment Syndrome risk)

Primary_Symptoms: Chronic regional muscle pain characterized by hyperirritable spots ('trigger points') within taut bands of skeletal muscle that refer pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Local twitch response on snapping palpation; Referred pain patterns; Muscle stiffness; Restricted ROM; Sleep disruption
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Manspeshi me kadi ganth (trigger point) choone par doosri jagah tez dard jata hai?; 2. Pith, gardan ya kandhe me purana dard hai?; 3. Dabane par 'jhatka' lagta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Trigger Point Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD (if severe spasm); Trigger point dry needling / local anesthetic injection (specialist-administered); Physical therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC. Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Muscle relaxants Rx only, max 5-7 days (drowsiness caution, contraindicated in pregnancy). Trigger point injections Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Apply moist warm compresses over trigger points for 15 mins twice daily; Use a foam roller or tennis ball for gentle self-myofascial release; Perform daily passive muscle stretching; Maintain proper posture
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation (palpation of taut band and local twitch response); ESR/CRP (normal in MPS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive motor deficit; Unexplained fever or weight loss; Pain non-responsive to conservative therapy

Primary_Symptoms: Aching pain in temporomandibular joint (in front of ear), jaw muscles, or temple; Exacerbated by chewing, yawning, or wide opening
Secondary_Symptoms: Joint clicking, popping, or crepitus; Restricted jaw opening (trismus); Lockjaw; Tonal tinnitus; Morning jaw muscle fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana chabane, jamai lene, ya muuh kholne par jabde (ear ke aage) me dard hota hai?; 2. Muuh kholte waqt 'click' ya charcharahat ki awaaz aati hai?; 3. Raat me daant piisne (bruxism) ki aadat hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Ibuprofen
Supportive_Medicines: Soft diet; Night guard occlusal splint (Dentist-fitted); Moist heat compress; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-5 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, asthma, 3rd trimester pregnancy. Intra-articular TMJ steroid injections or night guards Rx under dental specialist
Home_Care_Advice: Eat soft foods (khichdi, soups, mashed foods); Avoid chewing gum, hard foods, and wide yawning; Apply warm moist compress to jaw for 10 mins 3 times daily; Wear dentist-fitted night guard if grinding teeth
Lab_Investigations: X-ray TMJ (Open and Closed mouth views); MRI TMJ (evaluates articular disc displacement); Dental occlusal evaluation
Emergency_Red_Flags: Complete lockjaw (inability to open or close mouth); High fever with severe facial/jaw swelling; Ear discharge

Primary_Symptoms: Acute/subacute onset of severe symmetrical pain and stiffness in shoulder and pelvic girdles in elderly patients (>50 years, peak 70y)
Secondary_Symptoms: Profound MORNING STIFFNESS >45 MINS; Difficulty rising from chair or combing hair; Systemic symptoms: low fever, fatigue, weight loss
Typical_Duration: Months to 2 years (requires slow steroid taper)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Umar 50 se zyada hai aur dono kandho va kulho me subah uthte hi severe aedan rehti hai?; 2. Kurse se uthne ya baal banane me takleef hai?; 3. Kankhi (temple) me sirdard ya aankh me dhundla-pan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Low-dose Oral Systemic Corticosteroids - Prednisolone under Rheumatologist)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (1 to 2 years slow taper)
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 600 IU daily; Bisphosphonates (for steroid-induced osteoporosis prevention); PPI cover
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Oral corticosteroids require strict monitoring of blood glucose, BP, bone density, and infection risk. Never stop steroids abruptly (risk of adrenal crisis). HIGH RISK OF CO-EXISTING GIANT CELL ARTERITIS (temporal arteritis)
Home_Care_Advice: Take oral prednisolone strictly as prescribed every morning with food; Never skip doses or stop abruptly; Take Calcium and Vitamin D3 daily; Regular blood tests for ESR/CRP
Lab_Investigations: ESR (>50 mm/hr, often >100) and CRP (markedly elevated - diagnostic hallmark); Complete Blood Count (normocytic anemia); Temporal Artery Biopsy / Ultrasound (if GCA suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: SUDDEN VISION LOSS, DOUBLE VISION, UNILATERAL TEMPORAL HEADACHE, OR JAW CLAUDICATION WHILE CHEWING (Giant Cell Arteritis emergency - immediate high-dose IV steroids needed to prevent permanent blindness)

Primary_Symptoms: Symmetrical inflammatory polyarthritis affecting small joints of hands (MCP, PIP) and feet (MTP); MORNING STIFFNESS >1 HOUR
Secondary_Symptoms: Joint swelling, warmth, and tenderness; Sparing of DIP joints; Fatigue; Low-grade fever; Rheumatoid nodules
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haatho aur pairo ke chhote jodon me dono taraf soojan aur dard hai?; 2. Subah uthne par 1 ghante se zyada aedan rehti hai?; 3. RA factor ya Anti-CCP test hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - rheumatologist supervision required (Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs - **Methotrexate** ONCE A WEEK / Leflunomide / Sulfasalazine)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 7.5 to 15 mg Methotrexate **ONCE A WEEK ONLY**
Supportive_Medicines: Folic Acid 5 mg (taken on non-methotrexate days, e.g., Tuesday); Low-dose short-term Prednisolone bridge; NSAIDs SOS for acute pain
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - rheumatologist supervision required. **METHOTREXATE IS TAKEN ONCE A WEEK, NEVER DAILY (DAILY DOSING CAN BE FATAL DUE TO SEVERE BONE MARROW SUPPRESSION AND TOXICITY)**. Folic acid cover mandatory. Regular CBC and LFT monitoring mandatory. Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy (teratogenic)
Home_Care_Advice: Take Methotrexate strictly ONCE A WEEK on fixed chosen day; Take Folic acid on non-methotrexate days as advised; Never double doses; Perform gentle joint range-of-motion exercises; Stop smoking completely
Lab_Investigations: Anti-CCP (Anti-Cyclic Citrullinated Peptide - highly specific); Rheumatoid Factor (RF); ESR and CRP; Complete Blood Count; LFT and RFT; X-rays Hands and Feet
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with single hot, red, extremely swollen joint (Septic Arthritis superinfection suspicion); Breathlessness or dry cough (Rheumatoid ILD); Severe leukopenia/fever

Primary_Symptoms: Inflammatory arthritis in patients with Psoriasis; Asymmetric oligoarthritis or symmetric polyarthritis; Dactylitis ('sausage digit')
Secondary_Symptoms: Enthesitis (heel pain/Achilles tendinitis); Psoriatic skin plaques; Nail pitting/onycholysis; Spondylitis (inflammatory back pain); DIP joint involvement
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Skin par Psoriasis (safed patti waala daad) hai ya naakhun kharab hain?; 2. Ungli me poori tarah soojan ('sausage finger') aayi hai?; 3. Aedi ya jodon me dard hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - rheumatologist supervision required (DMARDs - **Methotrexate** ONCE A WEEK / Sulfasalazine / Apremilast / Biologics - TNF/IL-17 Inhibitors)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 7.5 to 20 mg Methotrexate **ONCE A WEEK ONLY** / 30 mg (Apremilast)
Supportive_Medicines: Folic Acid 5 mg (taken on non-methotrexate days); NSAIDs short-term for symptomatic pain; Topical antipsoriatic agents
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - rheumatologist supervision required. **METHOTREXATE IS TAKEN ONCE A WEEK, NEVER DAILY (DAILY DOSING CAN BE FATAL)**. Folic acid cover mandatory. Regular CBC and LFT monitoring required. Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy
Home_Care_Advice: Take Methotrexate strictly ONCE A WEEK; Use gentle joint protection techniques; Maintain skin moisturization; Perform low-impact aerobic exercise (swimming/cycling); Stop smoking
Lab_Investigations: Anti-CCP and RF (usually negative - seronegative arthritis); ESR/CRP; X-rays affected joints (pencil-in-cup deformity in late stage); Dermatological skin evaluation
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with acute red hot swollen joint (Septic arthritis rule out); Severe erythroderma skin flare; Ocular pain/redness (Uveitis)

Primary_Symptoms: Asymmetric inflammatory oligoarthritis predominantly affecting lower extremity large joints (knee, ankle) 1-4 weeks after GI or GU infection
Secondary_Symptoms: Triad (Reiter's): Arthritis + Urethritis/Cervicitis + Conjunctivitis; Enthesitis (heel pain); Dactylitis; Circinate balanitis; Keratoderma blennorrhagicum
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Joint pain shuru hone se 1-4 hafte pehle dast (diarrhea) ya peshab me jalan (STD/UTI) hui thi?; 2. Ghutne ya ganth me soojan hai?; 3. Aankh me lalapan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: NSAIDs (Naproxen / Indomethacin) + Antibiotics (for active underlying GU infection)
Supportive_Medicines: Sulfasalazine 500 mg BD (if chronic non-resolving >3 months under rheumatologist); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Intra-articular steroid injection
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs full anti-inflammatory dose after food under doctor guidance. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure. Treat underlying active Chlamydial GU infection in patient and sexual partner
Home_Care_Advice: Rest inflamed joints during acute phase; Apply ice packs for 15 mins 3 times daily; Perform gentle passive range of motion as pain improves; Practice safe sex barrier precautions
Lab_Investigations: Urine PCR for Chlamydia trachomatis; Stool culture (Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, Yersinia); HLA-B27 testing; ESR/CRP; Joint fluid aspiration (sterile)
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with purulent joint effusion; Ocular pain with severe photophobia (anterior uveitis); Cardiac conduction blocks (aortic regurgitation/heart block)

Primary_Symptoms: Acute onset severe monoarticular joint pain, swelling, warmth, intense erythema, and complete inability to bear weight or move joint
Secondary_Symptoms: High fever with rigors/chills; Extreme pseudoparalysis of limb; Joint held in flexion comfort posture; Irritability (in pediatric cases)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ek hi joint me achanak severe soojan, lalapan aur tez bukhar aaya hai?; 2. Joint ko thoda bhi hilane par severe painful cry hoti hai?; 3. Wazan tiktat nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Injection Vancomycin / Cloxacillin
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency IV bactericidal antibiotics + Surgical Joint Arthrotomy / Arthroscopic Lavage
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER Transfer; Emergency Joint Aspiration (Arthrocentesis); Emergency Surgical Drainage/Lavage; High-dose IV Antibiotics for 2-4 weeks
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening orthopedic surgical emergency with high risk of rapid irreversible cartilage destruction. DO NOT DELAY BY GIVING ORAL NSAIDS OR ANTIBIOTICS AT HOME. Do not force joint movement
Home_Care_Advice: Immobilize affected joint completely using a pillow or splint; Do NOT attempt to massage, stretch, or bear weight on joint; Transfer patient immediately to hospital emergency department
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Synovial Fluid Analysis (WBC >50,000/mcL with >90% PMNs, Gram stain, culture & sensitivity); Blood Cultures x 2; CBC; ESR & CRP (markedly elevated); Joint Ultrasound / Plain X-ray
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Septic shock signs (hypotension, confusion, cold clammy skin); High fever with rigors; Complete joint destruction signs

Common_Names_Hindi: Ghutne ki ghisai; Early Knee OA
Primary_Symptoms: Mechanical knee pain worsened by weight-bearing, walking, or climbing stairs and relieved by rest; Morning stiffness <30 minutes
Secondary_Symptoms: Fine crepitus on joint movement; Mild joint space tenderness; Localized joint effusion after heavy activity; Bony enlargement (Heberden/Bouchard nodes if generalized)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ghutne me dard chalne ya siidhiya chadne par badhta hai aur baithne par aaram milta hai?; 2. Subah uthne par 15-20 min aedan rehti hai?; 3. Ghutne me charcharahat (crepitus) aati hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel + Quadriceps Exercise
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Topical NSAID gel; Quadriceps strengthening exercises; Weight loss management; Glucosamine/Chondroitin (limited clinical evidence)
Precautions_Contraindications: First-line therapy: exercise, weight loss, and physiotherapy. Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Oral NSAIDs short course (3-5 days) after food for acute flares. Glucosamine/Chondroitin have limited clinical evidence and should not replace exercise/weight loss. Do not use repeated oral NSAIDs long-term
Home_Care_Advice: Perform daily isometric quadriceps strengthening and straight-leg raise exercises; Aim for weight loss if overweight (reduces knee load by 4x body weight); Use low-impact exercise (swimming/cycling); Avoid squatting, sitting cross-legged on floor, and frequent stair climbing
Lab_Investigations: Weight-bearing Standing X-ray Both Knees AP and Lateral views (shows mild joint space narrowing, early subchondral sclerosis)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe hot red joint swelling with high fever (Septic Arthritis suspicion); Inability to bear any weight following minor fall (fracture risk); Knee locking

Common_Names_Hindi: Severe Ghutne ki ghisai; Late Knee OA
Primary_Symptoms: Severe unremitting knee pain, rest pain, nocturnal awakening pain, and severe functional walking limitation; Marked crepitus and deformity
Secondary_Symptoms: Genu varum (bow-legged) deformity; Severe bony enlargement; Marked joint space loss; Flexion contracture; Frequent instability
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ghutne me severe ghisai batayi hai?; 2. Raat ko sote me aur baithne par bhi ghutne me tez dard hota hai?; 3. Ghutne bahar ki taraf tedhe (bow-legs) ho gaye hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Intra-articular Hyaluronic Acid / Corticosteroid Injection / Total Knee Arthroplasty - TKA Evaluation)
Dosage_Frequency: Intra-articular injection by Orthopedic Surgeon as indicated
Supportive_Medicines: Custom knee orthotic brace; Intra-articular Hyaluronic acid viscosupplementation; Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA Surgery)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Oral NSAIDs should NOT be used as continuous long-term daily therapy due to high cardiovascular, renal, and peptic ulcer risks in elderly patients. Intra-articular steroid/viscosupplementation injections Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Use a walking stick held in opposite hand to offload joint; Modify living space (western toilet, avoid stairs); Perform non-weight-bearing quadriceps exercises; Maintain healthy weight
Lab_Investigations: Weight-bearing Standing X-rays Both Knees (AP, Lateral, and Rosenberg views - shows severe joint space collapse, large osteophytes, subchondral cysts)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Joint infection signs post intra-articular injection (fever, purulent swelling); Complete knee locking or sudden collapse/fall

Primary_Symptoms: Deep groin pain radiating to anterior thigh or knee, worsened by weight-bearing and walking; Reduced internal rotation of hip
Secondary_Symptoms: Antalgic gait (limping); Stiffness on rising from chair; Difficulty tying shoelaces or putting on socks; Crepitus
